questions.q: Why is User License selected before Profile on the New User form?
options: It's purely alphabetical ordering with no functional relationship
The license determines which profiles are even available to select
Profile must be set first in every other version of the form
License can be changed after Save but Profile cannot
questions.explain: License limits the pool of available profiles, so Salesforce requires it to be chosen first.

questions.q: A feature isn't included in a user's license. Can a profile or permission set still unlock it for that user?
options: Yes, profiles override license restrictions
No — a feature not included in the license can't be unlocked by profile or permission set
Only permission sets can override a license, not profiles
Only if the user is a System Administrator
questions.explain: License sets the outer boundary of what's possible; profiles and permission sets configure access within that boundary, not beyond it.

questions.q: What does a license represent, as distinct from a profile?
options: The broad category of access purchased for a user, versus the specific permissions an admin configures
They are two names for the exact same setting
A license only applies to Experience Cloud sites
A license is assigned after a permission set, never before
questions.explain: A license is what the organization purchased for a user; a profile is the admin-configured baseline permissions within what that license allows.

questions.q: Why could a Chatter Free licensed user never be assigned a permission set that requires a Salesforce license?
options: Permission sets ignore license requirements entirely
A permission set's own license requirement is a gate independent of the user's profile
Chatter Free users cannot be assigned any permission sets under any circumstances
This is only true in Salesforce Classic, not Lightning
questions.explain: Permission sets carry their own License field, and a mismatch between that and the user's license blocks assignment regardless of profile.

questions.q: What happens to a license seat when a user is deactivated?
options: It's permanently lost and cannot be reused
It remains occupied forever, even for deactivated users
It becomes free for reassignment to another user
It automatically converts to a different license type
questions.explain: Deactivating a user frees their license seat, letting the organization reassign it — one reason deactivation (not deletion) is the correct offboarding step.
